summary: Redwood AE/SE team walked Lumen Health through the Redwood Console usage analytics and per-route cost breakdown. Main ask: show how per-route dashboards can surface token and model costs, support billing allocation, and help decide hosted vs dedicated. Customer requested pricing, security docs, and a POC using two high-volume routes. Action items and dates agreed.
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-04-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Narayanan (CTO, Lumen), Evan Brooks (Product), Sofia Martinez (Infra)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm maya, i'm the AE on the account, and liam's our solutions engineer.
[00:06] Liam O'Rourke: hi all, thanks for the time, i'll take the console walk and then we can dig into the per-route cost questions, and any security stuff.
[00:12] Dr. Priya Narayanan: thanks, yeah we're mostly focused on two things—understanding live cost by route and making sure we can map cost back to product teams.
[00:20] Evan Brooks: also want to see latency breakdowns per model, and how rollout A/B's look in the console.
[00:25] Sofia Martinez: and critically for infra, can we see egress, KMS usage, and what data leaves our VPC if we do private deploy.
[00:33] Liam O'Rourke: absolutely. quick agenda on my screen — usage overview, per-route dashboards, token-level cost, then rollouts and alerts.
[00:40] [Screen share starts — Redwood Consol (note: transcription sometimes shows 'Consol')]
[00:45] Liam O'Rourke: starting with the usage analytics page — this is aggregated across models and routes. you can filter by time window, customer, and deployment mode — hosted, dedicated, private.
[00:55] Liam O'Rourke: here we show tokens in, tokens out, total inference cost estimate, and cost per 1k tokens. the engine backfills model-specific kernel efficiency so you see not only tokens but expected GPU cost.
[01:08] Evan Brooks: is that cost a raw cloud cost or does it include Redwood overhead?
[01:12] Maya Chen: good question — by default it's Redwood estimated cost (infrastructure + runtime overhead) but you can toggle to show just raw infra burn (what you'd pay to cloud) or unit-cost after our platform discounts.
[01:22] Sofia Martinez: can we map that to our internal charge codes?
[01:25] Liam O'Rourke: yes, we have per-route tags and you can export csv or hook to our cost-allocation API. in the per-route dashboard you'll see tag-based breakdowns.
[01:35] [00:60] Dr. Priya Narayanan: show us a per-route example — like our triage-route vs summary-route.
[01:40] Liam O'Rourke: switching to Routes — here's a route list. you can click into a route and see token distribution, model versions used, average latency P50/P95, and token-cost over time.
[01:53] Liam O'Rourke: note the token-level cost is computed per model variant and includes batching & prefix cache effects. so if a route is hitting the KV cash (sic) heavily your per-token cost drops here.
[02:05] Evan Brooks: KV cash? did you mean KV cache — yeah that explains the lower cost on triage. nice.
[02:10] [02:15] Maya Chen: there's also a 'cost allocation' view where you can split cost by team or product by assigning tags or weights to routes. customers use this to bill internal teams.
[02:23] Sofia Martinez: how granular are the timestamps? we need to reconcile with our observability — can we export raw events?
[02:29] Liam O'Rourke: full event export is available for dedicated and private; hosted has a sampling window to keep queries fast. exports come as newline-delimited json or csv with per-request tokens, model, latency, node id.
[02:41] Dr. Priya Narayanan: i heard 'dedicated and private' a couple times — for compliance, we'd prefer private but want to understand unit economics vs hosted. can you show effective cost differences?
[02:53] Liam O'Rourke: sure — back to the cost overview: you can pick 'deployment mode' and we show normalized cost per 1M tokens. dedicated capacity drops unit cost because of reserved GPU amortization, private on-prem depends on your hardware input. we also surface break-even points based on your monthly token volume.
[03:10] Evan Brooks: can we plug in our own GPU cost and utilization numbers?
[03:13] Liam O'Rourke: yes, under settings > cost models you can override spot/on-demand pricing, blob storage egress assumptions, and KMS per-request costs.
[03:21] Maya Chen: quick interjection — customers commonly upload a sample traffic profile and we run a 7-day synthetic model to produce expected spend; liam will share the spreadsheet with the calc.
[03:30] [03:35] Dr. Priya Narayanan: security — SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS, audit logs. how does console show audit trails?
[03:43] Liam O'Rourke: audit logs are in the console under 'activity' with user, action, and request context; we persist with retention settings for enterprise. for private we can integrate with your SIEM. we support SSO/SAML and scoped API keys with RBAC.
[03:56] Sofia Martinez: KMS — is key material ever in Redwood control plane?
[03:59] Maya Chen: for private customers you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and we can support HSM-backed KMS; for hosted, we manage keys but offer CMKs and customer-managed key options where permitted. we can send our security pack.
[04:12] [04:18] Evan Brooks: back to rollouts — we want to run canaries and measure cost impact of switching models. how is that surfaced?
[04:25] Liam O'Rourke: rollout page shows per-variant traffic %, latency and cost delta. you can annotate experiments and auto-failover to a cheaper model if latency goes above threshold.
[04:34] Dr. Priya Narayanan: does the console show sampling of generated outputs for quality guardrails?
[04:38] Liam O'Rourke: yes, we surface sampled outputs and attach prompt/eval tags so you can connect regressions to particular rollouts and trigger quality monitors.
[04:46] [04:50] Maya Chen: common objection we see: "we don't trust vendor cost numbers" — we recommend running a short POC with your traffic and we'll produce token-level mapping plus raw infra burn so you can compare.
[04:59] Evan Brooks: ok that feels fair. what do you need from us to scope the POC?
[05:03] Liam O'Rourke: ideally two weeks of representative logs or a synthetic profile (RPS + distribution of seq lengths), route config names, and SLA targets. we'll run bench and return a per-route cost model.
[05:14] Sofia Martinez: our privacy team will insist on NDA before sharing logs — is that okay?
[05:18] Maya Chen: absolutely. we'll route through legal; for the POC we can also accept anonymized traffic.
[05:24] [05:30] Dr. Priya Narayanan: timeline — we're targeting a Q2 decision for hosted vs dedicated.
[05:33] Maya Chen: that aligns — we'll try to get pricing to you by the 18th so you can review with procurement.
[05:38] Evan Brooks: curious on multi-region cost — we do traffic split across US/EU, can console break down per-region?
[05:44] Liam O'Rourke: yes region is a primary dimension; we show per-region token cost and also routing policies so you can compare routing to closest region vs central model.
[05:52] [06:00] Maya Chen: ok quick recap — action items: maya send pricing & security docs; liam send benchmark spreadsheet and recording; lumen to share anonymized route traffic and target metrics. p o c kickoff week of the 27th if that works.
[06:10] Dr. Priya Narayanan: works for us. thanks — that was helpful.
[06:15] Maya Chen: cool thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.

Notes on transcript: occasional transcript noise, speaker labels simplified. references: shared doc "Lumen POC traffic template" (link sent after), "Redwood security pack" (link).
